title: Amboseli elephant deaths:  Kenya Wildlife Service launches urgent inquiry after 14 carcasses found
excerpt: It is the highest number of elephant deaths to be recorded in this area of southern Kenya in decades.
content_html:
An urgent investigation has been launched into the mysterious deaths of 15 elephants in southern Kenya near the Amboseli National Park.

The Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) told the BBC that experts were examining the carcasses and said that tissue samples had been sent to laboratories to determine whether the deaths were caused by disease, poisoning or another factor.

The park and its surrounds are known as the Amboseli ecosystem, a vast area that straddles the border with Tanzania, which is famous for its wildlife.

Officials say this is the first time in decades that elephant mortalities on this scale have been recorded in the region where they have successfully cracked down on poaching.

KWS says there is currently no evidence pointing to a single cause of death.

The carcasses include elephants of different ages and sexes, suggesting the deaths are not limited to a single family or demographic.

The KWS said the deaths occurred over a month between 24 June and 24 July 2026.

The wildlife authorities also confirmed to the BBC all the deaths had been recorded outside the Amboseli National Park.

Earlier, KWS's head of communication Duncan Wanyama told local media the bodies had been found at different locations surrounding the park, around 15km (nine miles) to 30km from its boundaries.

According to figures from the Amboseli Trust for Elephants, which monitors the movements of the animals, there were more than 2,000 elephants in the Amboseli ecosystem as of 2025.

content_html_zh:
肯尼亚南部安博塞利国家公园附近15头大象神秘死亡事件已启动紧急调查。

肯尼亚野生动物管理局（KWS）告诉英国广播公司，专家正在检查尸体，并表示组织样本已送往实验室，以确定死亡是否是由疾病、中毒或其他因素造成的。

该公园及其周边地区被称为安博塞利生态系统，这是一个横跨坦桑尼亚边境的广阔区域，坦桑尼亚以其野生动物而闻名。

官员们表示，在他们成功打击偷猎的地区，数十年来首次出现如此大规模的大象死亡事件。

KWS 表示，目前没有证据表明死亡原因是单一的。

这些尸体包括不同年龄和性别的大象，这表明死亡并不局限于单个家庭或人口。

KWS表示，死亡事件发生在2026年6月24日至7月24日的一个月内。

野生动物管理局还向英国广播公司证实，所有死亡事件均发生在安博塞利国家公园外。

早些时候，KWS 的通讯主管 Duncan Wanyama 告诉当地媒体，在公园周围的不同地点发现了尸体，距离公园边界约 15 公里（9 英里）至 30 公里。

根据监测动物活动的安博塞利大象信托基金的数据，截至 2025 年，安博塞利生态系统中有超过 2,000 头大象。
